title: The LALA Benchmark: Evaluating Literary and Linguistic Analysis in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.34080v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We introduce the Literature and Linguistics Analysis Benchmark (LALA), comprising 236 open-ended questions written by experts in linguistics and literary studies, together with expert-provided ideal answers. By comparing models within families and at similar training scales using human and LLM judges, LALA identifies differences in linguistic competence associated with post-training, offering a framework for evaluating future models and guiding targeted improvements. We administered questions to 17 language models and evaluated their responses using both human expert assessment and two LLM evaluators, Sol and Qwen. Base models displayed little of the linguistic competence assessed by the benchmark, whereas their post-trained versions performed markedly better, suggesting that post-training plays a central role in making linguistic knowledge accessible and usable. translated_title: LALA基准：评估大语言模型中的文学与语言学分析能力
translated_abstract: 我们推出了文学与语言学分析基准（LALA），其中包含236道由语言学和文学研究领域专家撰写的开放式问题，并附有专家提供的理想答案。通过使用人类评委和大语言模型评委，在同一模型家族内及相似训练规模下对模型进行比较，LALA识别出了与后训练相关的语言能力差异，为评估未来模型和指导针对性改进提供了一个框架。我们对17个语言模型进行了测试，并采用人类专家评估和两个大语言模型评估器（Sol和Qwen）对其回答进行了评价。结果显示，基座模型几乎不具备该基准所考察的语言能力，而经过后训练的版本表现显著更好，这表明后训练在使语言知识变得可获取和可用方面发挥着核心作用。相比之下，参数量与语言能力之间未显示出统计学上的显著关联。
tldr: LALA基准通过236道专家撰写的文学与语言学开放式问题评估17个大语言模型，发现后训练（而非参数量）是使模型具备可用的语言能力的关键因素。
en_tdlr: The LALA benchmark evaluates 17 LLMs with 236 expert-written open-ended literary and linguistic questions, revealing that post-training (rather than parameter count) is the key factor in making linguistic knowledge accessible and usable in models.
